## Summary
The release workflow remembers that a run once needed approval and reports that historical state as the timeout cause, even after all reported approval attempts succeeded. This sends maintainers toward an already-completed action rather than the currently queued checks.

## Tested version and evidence
- Workflow commit: `af6fb9fd46b12b637c264cebad03c47ee071bd35` (package.json version `2026.11.1`), preparing release `2026.11.04` in [PR #196](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-presets/pull/196).
- [Observed job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-presets/actions/runs/41869788740/job/126713412858), November 4, 2026 UTC:
  - 17:36:14–15: successful approval messages for runs `41878837109`, `41878836924`, `41878836893`.
  - 18:05:57: merge refusal says two of three required status checks are queued; the settling set is `test (22), codeql, test (26), simulation-release-gates`, with no failing check reported.
  - 18:05:58: timeout nevertheless says the CI run is awaiting workflow approval and asks a maintainer to approve it once.
- [Exact workflow source](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-presets/blob/af6fb9fd46b12b637c264cebad03c47ee071bd35/.github/workflows/release.yml#L378-L490): `awaiting_approval` starts at zero outside the polling loop, becomes one whenever pending runs were seen, and is never reset after successful approval or a later empty pending-run poll. The deadline branch tests this sticky flag.

## Source goal
[Canonical pm-g33z](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-presets/blob/af6fb9fd46b12b637c264cebad03c47ee071bd35/.agents/pm/issues/pm-g33z.toon) explicitly says the merge wait should detect parked runs and distinguish awaiting approval from failed checks in the deadline error. Preserve its protected-merge-before-publication ordering.

## Isolated reproduction
A local shell probe exercises the exact deadline conditional, with no GitHub requests, merge, approval, publication or tagging:
1. Initialize `awaiting_approval=0`.
2. Model a poll that discovers a pending run, successfully approves it and sets `awaiting_approval=1` as the current source does.
3. Model a later poll with `pending_runs=""`, while merge remains blocked on settling checks.
4. Enter the timeout branch. It still prints the awaiting-approval error.

This independently establishes the diagnostic branch defect. It does not establish why the hosted checks remained queued or claim that approval caused the timeout.

## Expected and actual behavior
Expected: timeout describes the latest observed approval/check/review state, includes actionable links for approval only if approval remains pending, and distinguishes a failed observation from a verified empty pending set.

Actual: any earlier approval requirement permanently selects the approval-specific timeout message, suppressing the settling/failing summary even after successful approval.

Impact: misleading remediation and avoidable maintainer effort. The workflow failed closed here; this is not evidence of an unsafe publication or of npm publication success.

## Acceptance and regression criteria
- Recompute pending-approval state per successful poll or explicitly verify approval state at timeout. Do not infer current state merely from a previous approval attempt.
- Cover pending -> approval succeeds -> no pending runs -> unrelated checks queued: timeout must report queued/settling checks, not request approval.
- Cover genuine still-pending or denied approval: timeout retains the correct run link and remedy.
- Cover API/read failure separately from a verified no-pending response.
- Preserve protected merge, required reviews/checks and publication/tagging gates; no bypasses or automatic policy relaxation.

## Duplicate check and limits
Checked all 197 current all-status GitHub issue/PR entries and all 89 canonical TOON records at the tested commit. No existing pm-presets issue owns this stale timeout diagnostic; #194 is a separate coverage failure and pm-g33z is the original release-ordering work. The sibling diagnostic is already tracked in [pm-changelog #320](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-changelog/issues/320). No full workflow replay or production mutation performed.
Release timeout reports stale approval state after successful automatic approvals
